item.title: The Federal Reserve raises interest rates by a quarter percentage point
item.description: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in more than three years Wednesday.
item.content:encoded: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in more than three years Wednesday.

item.title: Economist explains the Fed's decision to raise interest rates
item.description: NPR's A Martinez speaks with economist Claudia Sahm about why the Federal Reserve chose to raise interest rates after months of keeping them steady.

item.title: What the Fed rate hike means for pocketbooks and politics
item.description: The Federal Reserve's decision to raise interest rates has broader political and economic implications, with affordability top of mind for voters ahead of the midterms.

item.title: Fed raises interest rates for first time in more than three years
item.description: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates today Wednesday the first time in more than three years. The central bank is trying to curb stubborn inflation, which was rekindled by the war with Iran.
item.content:encoded: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates today Wednesday the first time in more than three years. The central bank is trying to curb stubborn inflation, which was rekindled by the war with Iran.

item.title: The Fed is expected to raise interest rates. What it means for consumers?
item.description: Mark Zandi, chief economist with Moody's Analytics, talks about the Federal Reserve's expected decision to raise interest rates and the implications of that move.

item.title: The Fed raises interest rates for the first time in over three years
item.description: The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate Wednesday to combat stubborn inflation. That will make it more expensive to borrow money to buy a car or carry a balance on a credit card.

item.title: Turkish habit of stashing gold "under the pillow' hurts economy, government says
item.description: For years, Turks have stashed their gold at home against a raining day, mistrustful of banks. Now the government says that tradition hurts the economy

item.title: CBO says Iran war driving up inflation, puts price tag at $38 billion
item.description: Two new, independent reports show detailed looks at the costs of the war in Iran. It's led to shortages in U.S. weapons, supply chain bottlenecks and a price tag in the tens of billions of dollars.

item.title: Family income rose and poverty fell in 2025 — but safety net cuts could erase gains
item.description: An annual report from the Census Bureau shows the average family made more money in 2025 than the year before, while the official poverty rate declined. Health care coverage was little changed from 2024.
